summary: The unit tests cover core functionality well (parsing, bumping, file I/O, changelog generation, CLI smoke test) with clear organization and good pytest usage. However, the test suite fails to meet a critical explicit requirement: 'ALL TESTS MUST RUN THROUGH ACT.' There are no tests that (1) set up temp git repos, (2) invoke `act push --rm`, (3) capture output to `act-result.txt`, (4) parse and assert exact expected values, or (5) verify job success. The test_workflow_structure.py tests the YAML but does not execute the workflow. Edge case coverage is also limited (no 0.0.0 version, changelog accumulation, whitespace variations, or BREAKING-CHANGE hyphenated variant despite implementation). Missing fixture files (commits_*.txt) and the workflow file itself are not shown, so tests depending on them will fail. The suite would catch regressions in the Python module but not in the actual CI/CD pipeline—the whole point of the GitHub Actions workflow requirement.
